Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12745 of 2022
Applicant :- Smt. Mamta

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Bhushan Yadav,Krishna Pratap Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mukesh Joshi Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 876 of 2022, under sections 354 Gha, 328, 376, 511, 323, 504, 506, 420 I.P.C. and 7/8 POCSO Act Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad.

entities.text: POCSO Act Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Facts in brief are that applicant is mother of co-accused Deepak who is said to have enticed away the daughter of the informant who was minor and got the marriage registered before the Marriage Registration Officer.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant has falsely been implicated by the informant as being mother of co-accused Deepak.

Allegedly she is said to have Smt. Mamta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144677635/
1 administered intoxicant on the victim and got the papers signed by her though there is no any such evidence on record to show the complicity of present applicant.

entities.text: Smt. Mamta vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that before the Marriage Registration Officer, the co-accused Deepak and the victim both were present then registration was made.
The Authority concerned registered the marriage on getting it verified that both are major and consenting party.
In this way, it cannot be said that she was under the influence of intoxicant.
Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case applicant is mother of co-accused Deepak at the instance of whom the marriage was entered into by Deepak with the victim who was minor at the time of alleged marriage, therefore, she is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by both the parties as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, there appears good ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.
In default of any of the conditions, this order will automatically stand vacated.
